subject: Computer Networking
title: Home Network Switches
description: A short lesson to help you apply Home Network Switches.

hook.text: Your router has four Ethernet ports. But you have eight wired devices. Add a switch.

buildup.text: A switch expands wired connections. Plug it into your router and gain 8, 16, or more ports.

discovery.text: Unlike a hub, a switch learns which device is on which port. It sends data only to the right one.

twist.text: Managed switches support VLANs and traffic monitoring. Unmanaged ones are pure plug-and-play.

climax.text: Some switches support PoE — delivering data and electrical power through a single cable.

punchline.text: A switch is a smart splitter. More ports, same speed.

quiz.question: What advantage does a switch have over a hub?
options: It sends data only to the correct destination port

details.summary: A network switch connects multiple devices on the same local network, forwarding frames only to the specific port where the destination device is connected. Unlike hubs that broadcast everything everywhere, switches learn device locations and send traffic intelligently.
details.whyItMatters: Switches are the core of every wired network. Understanding how they differ from hubs and routers clarifies how local network traffic flows efficiently between devices.
takeaways: Switches forward frames to specific ports using MAC addresses
A MAC address table maps device addresses to physical ports
Unmanaged switches work out of the box with no configuration

faq.question: What is the difference between a switch and a hub?
faq.answer: A hub broadcasts every frame to all ports, wasting bandwidth and creating collisions. A switch learns which devices are on which ports and forwards frames only to the correct destination port. Switches are faster, more secure, and have completely replaced hubs in modern networks.

faq.question: Do I need a network switch at home?
faq.answer: If you have more wired devices than your router has Ethernet ports, a switch adds extra ports. Plug the switch into the router and connect devices to the switch. Gigabit unmanaged switches are inexpensive and require zero configuration.
